docs.text: Welcome to the Celtic Sea NEMO model Github wiki! Overview This guide described the process of building a regional NEMO model covers the Celtic Sea. The setup is designed for the Cirrus HPC system (https://www.cirrus.ac.uk/), and the setup procedure is largely the same as that previously used on ARCHER2. The compilation workflow referenced a NEMO building script provided by Sarah Wakelin. Many forcing generation methods and scripts were provided by other modellers and will be acknowledged in the following description. If you are using a different HPC system, you may need to adapt the compilation and execution procedures. Note that the same model configuration may produce slightly different outputs on different systems owing to differences in floating-point calculations, compilers, MPI libraries and process counts. Here, we provide an automated deployment script alongside explanation of each configuration step. There is a mirror website which reflect similar documenting content in https://binguo999.github.io/CelticSea1.5/ Model Summary Celtic Sea 1.5 covers the Celtic Sea and surrounding shelf waters, from approximately 9.31°W to 0.14°E and 48.32°N to 52.70°N, as shown in the map below. The model grid is a direct cutout of AMM15 with 1.5 km horizontal resolution but with 30 sigma vertical levels. Featuring: FES2014 tides Open boundary forcing downscaled from the AMM7 reanalysis ERA5 Surface forcing River forcing achieved from Glofas dataset Initial condition (with Temperature and salinity) from the AMM7 reanalysis Wetting and drying in shallow coastal areas

docs.text: These instructions build the Celtic Sea 1.5 km ocean configuration on Cirrus using XIOS3 and NEMO 4.0.4 with GNU and MPICH. Build XIOS first. It supplies the library NEMO links against and the server executable launched alongside the model. Set up the paths and directories Start with a checkout of CelticSea1.5 git clone https://github.com/BinGuo999/CelticSea1.5.git cd CelticSea1.5 The core building scripts are in /SCRIPTS , where containing six numbered shell scripts that navigate the whole process of NEMO model building. In principle, the only file you need to editor is Scripts/1.make_path.sh (but in many cases minor issues arise and you need to make your relavent adaption). Open the file and check the following settings: Setting What to enter gituhb_download Absolute path to the CelticSea1.5 checkout. WDIR A writable directory on your directory, where everything happened. CONFIG NEMO configuration name (adapt it for your own model). Change NEMO_VER=NEMO_4.0.4 and HPC_TARG=cirrus-gnu-mpich for your own build. FORCING_DIR is a directory that containing the domain and forcing files for a test run. cd Scripts . ./1.make_path.sh . ./2.make_directories.sh The first script, 1.make_path.sh, sets and prints the paths. The 2.make_directories.sh, uses those paths to create the build and run folders. Build XIOS3 on Cirrus The XIOS build uses the shared files at /epccfs/n01/shared/xios3 . If you do not have the access to it, then you need to download the xios3 source code or use other version of xios like 2.5. Run the build from Scripts/ . . ./3.make_xios.sh The script loads PrgEnv-gnu and the parallel HDF5 and NetCDF modules. Use the same compiler and library environment for the NEMO build. The script copies XIOS to $XIOS_DIR and adapts the ARCHER2 settings for Cirrus. .fcm sets the compilers and build flags. .path tells XIOS where to find NetCDF and HDF5. .env contains only a comment because the script already loads the Cirrus modules. The script removes -lmpichf90 because the Fortran compiler wrapper ( ftn ) already adds the MPI library. The script then runs this command inside $XIOS_DIR . ./make_xios --prod --arch X86_CIRRUS-Gnu --netcdf_lib netcdf4_par --job 16 --full Check the build The script checks that the server is executable. echo "Executable is $XIOS_DIR/bin/xios_server.exe" Continue with 02. Compile NEMO once both files are present.
docs.title: 01. XIOS compilation

docs.text: Compile NEMO Complete 01. XIOS compilation first. NEMO links against the XIOS library built in that step. Run step 4 from Scripts/ . . ./4.make_nemo.sh The script loads the same GNU, parallel HDF5, and parallel NetCDF modules used to build XIOS. It also loads Subversion to check out NEMO 4.0.4 into $NEMO . Note Shared-library paths can vary between HPC systems, therefore you may need to adjust the library settings when building and running NEMO on another system. For example, the following command is commented out in this script: bash export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CRAY_LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH This command was required for this build on ARCHER2 but was unnecessary on Cirrus, where the loaded modules already configure the required shared-library paths. The script copies arch-cirrus-gnu-mpich.fcm into the NEMO checkout. This file tells NEMO which compiler and libraries to use. The script fills in $XIOS_DIR so the build can find the XIOS headers and library from step 3. It adds $CONFIG OCE to cfgs/work_cfgs.txt . This provides the configuration name and tells makenemo to include NEMO's ocean component ( OCE ). It copies the CelticSea1.5 customised Fortran files into the configuration's MY_SRC/ directory. When a local file has the same name as a standard NEMO source file, the build uses the local version. It copies cpp_co9-amm7.fcm to cpp_$CONFIG.fcm . This gives makenemo the compile-time options for this configuration. The key_mpp_mpi option lets NEMO run across multiple MPI processes, and key_iomput enables output through XIOS. ./makenemo -m $HPC_TARG -r $CONFIG -j 16 Check the executable After compilation, 4.make_nemo.sh checks whether nemo.exe is executable and prints its location if the check passes. test -x $CONFIG_DIR/BLD/bin/nemo.exe echo "Executable is $CONFIG_DIR/BLD/bin/nemo.exe" Continue with 03. Run the model to use the prepared 1993 inputs. To generate your own inputs, start with 04. NEMO tools compilation .
docs.title: 02. Compile NEMO

docs.text: Once you have compiled XIOS and NEMO, you can run the CelticSea1.5 test case. This guide describes the inputs needed for a fully forced run and where to download the model grid and sample forcing files. You can run the test now using these files, or work through the input generation steps first and return to this section later. You can also switch individual forcings on or off to build up the model setup gradually and check that each input works as expected. The following sections provide step-by-step instructions and scripts for generating the domain configuration file ( domain_cfg.nc ) and the required forcing inputs. Prepare the run directory In Scripts/1.make_path.sh , set FORCING_DIR to the path of the downloaded CelticSea1.5_input_1993 . The bundle contains domain_cfg.nc at its root, and input data in IC/ , OBC/ , SBC/ , River/ and TIDES/ . Prepare the test run from Scripts/ . . ./1.make_path.sh . ./6.make_test_run.sh cd $EXP The script copies the namelists, XIOS XML files and runnemo.slurm from RUN_DIRECTORIES/EXP_test_1993/ to $EXP . The default destination is $WDIR/RUN_DIRECTORY/CS1.5_1993_TEST . Use a fresh experiment directory for a new run. Step 6 copies over existing template files and stops if one of its symbolic links already exists. Path in the run directory Input domain_cfg.nc Celtic Sea grid and bathymetry information IC/ Temperature and salinity information on 1 January 1993 OBC/ Monthly open boundary files for 1993. The job also reads coordinates.bdy.nc for boundary grid information. SBC/ 1993 ERA5 forcing and both atmospheric interpolation weights. Keep the weights inside SBC/ , where NEMO reads them. river/ 1993 GloFAS runoff TIDES/ FES2014 tidal boundary files nemo.exe , xios_server.exe Links to the executables under $CONFIG_DIR/BLD/bin/ and $XIOS_DIR/bin/ , respectively Edit the namelist A namelist is a text file that set up the numerical options in NEMO model. namelist_ref supplies the default settings, and namelist_cfg supplies the settings for this specific experiment. In this configuration, namelist_cfg is regenerated from namelist.template for each month, allowing the simulation to run in monthly segments, with the output archived separately for each month. So, do not edit namelist_cfg , edit namelist.template . Some key namelist settings: - cn_domcfg = "./domain_cfg.nc" selects the Celtic Sea grid file. - rn_rdt = 80. sets an 80-second timestep. - ln_tsd_init = __INITS__ controls whether NEMO reads the initial temperature and salinity. The Slurm script sets it to .true. for the first month and .false. for restart months. - ln_blk = .true. enables the bulk formula for ERA5 surface forcing. - ln_rnf = .true. enables river runoff. - ln_bdy = .true. enables open boundary conditions. - ln_tide = .true. enables tidal forcing. Edit the Slurm script Modify runscript.slurm for your HPC environment (account details, queue, walltime, and core count). In the CelticSea1.5 hindcast, simulating January through December 1997 took about 1 hour and 50 minutes of wall-clock time on four Cirrus nodes (1 hour, 48 minutes and 11 seconds in Slurm job 630493 ). The variables iy1 and iy2 set the first and last simulation years. For the supplied 1993 run, ms=1 and end_month=12 select January through December, and nit0=1 starts at the first timestep. The first month reads the initial conditions. Each later month reads the restart from the previous month. The default tpd=1080 matches the 80-second timestep in the namelist. If you change rn_rdt , remember also update tpd to match the number of timesteps per day. Submit the experiment on Cirrus sbatch runnemo.slurm squeue -u your_user_name

docs.text: These internal NEMO tools in NEMO_VER/tools are used for NEMO input building or diagnosis and other additionalfunction. Here we build four a domain, prepare interpolation weights, and combine output split across MPI ranks. Here we provide the four Compile them after building NEMO , which installs the source tree and the Cirrus architecture file. Compile the tools Run the script from Scripts/ . . ./5.make_tools.sh The script loads the same GNU, HDF5 and NetCDF modules as the NEMO build. It makes two sets of source changes before compiling. It copies dom_oce.f90 , domain.f90 and domzgr.f90 from CS1.5_NEMO_support/DOMAINcfg_src/ into $TDIR/DOMAINcfg/src/ . These files add the Celtic Sea wetting and drying changes, including writing ht_wd and rn_wd_ref_depth to domain_cfg.nc . It applies the five WEIGHTS patches in CS1.5_NEMO_support/tool_patch_files/ . Find the executables maketools builds each tool with $HPC_TARG from 1.make_path.sh . Look for the results under $TDIR ( $NEMO/tools ). Tool Purpose Executables, relative to $TDIR NESTING Prepare nested coordinates, bathymetry and other inputs NESTING/BLD/bin/agrif_*.exe REBUILD_NEMO Combine files written separately by MPI ranks REBUILD_NEMO/BLD/bin/rebuild_nemo.exe WEIGHTS Prepare horizontal interpolation weights and remap fields for surface forcing WEIGHTS/BLD/bin/ contains scrip.exe , scripgrid.exe , scripinterp.exe and scripshape.exe DOMAINcfg Generate domain_cfg.nc from grid and bathymetry inputs DOMAINcfg/BLD/bin/make_domain_cfg.exe

docs.text: The Celtic Sea grid is a 426 × 312 cutout of the AMM15 GEG_SF12 grid. It uses Siddorn and Furner (2012) vertical stretching, with 31 levels and up to 30 wet levels, features with wetting and drying function. 1. Extract the coordinates and bathymetry The DOMAINcfg tool needs two inputs to build domain_cfg.nc . The coordinates file provides the horizontal grid, and the bathymetry file provides the water depth. For the Celtic Sea configuration, both are extracted from the AMM15 domain file, GEG_SF12.nc . Place GEG_SF12.nc or a link to it in $WDIR/BUILD_CFG/DOMAIN . From the checkout's Scripts/ directory, run the following in a Python environment with xarray and a NetCDF backend. . ./1.make_path.sh cd "$DOMAIN" python "$gituhb_download/BUILD_CFG/DOMAIN/cutout_bathy_subset.py" python "$gituhb_download/BUILD_CFG/DOMAIN/cutout_coordinates_subset.py" Both scripts extract the same 426 × 312 window using zero-based indices x = 500–925 and y = 244–555 , inclusive. The bathymetry script marks land and missing depths with -9999 , which is in line with WAD compatible bathymetry. The scripts write CelticS_coordinates.nc and CelticS_bathy_meter.nc . For more information on preparing coordinate and bathymetry files, see the SEVERN-SWOT guide to building a domain configuration file . 2. Generate and check domain_cfg.nc From the checkout's Scripts/ directory, load the paths and prepare the inputs in $TDIR/DOMAINcfg . . ./1.make_path.sh cd $TDIR/DOMAINcfg cp $gituhb_download/BUILD_CFG/DOMAIN/namelist_cfg . cp $gituhb_download/BUILD_CFG/DOMAIN/job_create_domain.slurm . ln -s BLD/bin/make_domain_cfg.exe . ln -s $DOMAIN/CelticS_coordinates.nc coordinates.nc ln -s $DOMAIN/CelticS_bathy_meter.nc bathy_meter.nc Use the namelist_ref and XML files already in the tool directory. The supplied namelist_cfg reads bathy_meter.nc ( nn_bathy = 1 ), selects Siddorn and Furner stretching ( ln_s_sf12 = .true. , rn_hc = 50 m), sets the wetting and drying reference depth to 0 m, and writes mesh_mask.nc ( nn_msh = 1 ). sbatch job_create_domain.slurm Once the job finishes, check the generated domain_cfg.nc in this $TDIR/DOMAINcfg .
docs.title: 05. Build domain configuration file

docs.text: Use pyBDY to interpolate FES2014 tidal harmonics onto the Celtic Sea 1.5 km open boundary. The September 2026 run in CELTIC8_GEE_SF12_cutout used the 426 × 312 GEG_SF12 domain from 05. Build domain configuration file . It produced amplitudes and phases for 24 tidal constituents and the boundary coordinates used to locate them on the NEMO grid. The 1993 test run already uses these harmonics from the forcing bundle. Follow this page to regenerate them. 1. Install pyBDY From a checkout of pyBDY, create the Conda environment and install the package. The environment file specifies Python 3.9. The NcML reader also needs Java. pyBDY repository conda env create -n pybdy -f environment.yml conda activate pybdy python -m pip install -e . pybdy -h 2. Prepare the input files Set ARCHIVED_RUN to the path of your copy of CELTIC8_GEE_SF12_cutout . Set DOMAIN_INPUTS to the directory containing the matching domain_cfg.nc and bathy_meter.nc , such as the backup_260921_GEG_SF12_cutout domain archive. The original links in the pyBDY archive point to ARCHER2 /work paths. Create fresh links to the Cirrus copies. From the Celtic Sea checkout's Scripts/ directory, load the paths and prepare a working directory. source ./1.make_path.sh ARCHIVED_RUN=/path/to/CELTIC8_GEE_SF12_cutout DOMAIN_INPUTS=/path/to/backup_260921_GEG_SF12_cutout mkdir -p "$WDIR/BUILD_CFG/OPEN_BOUNDARIES/GEG_SF12_cutout" cd "$WDIR/BUILD_CFG/OPEN_BOUNDARIES/GEG_SF12_cutout" cp "$ARCHIVED_RUN/namelist_AMM7CELTIC.bdy" . cp "$ARCHIVED_RUN/grid_name_map_sco.json" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/mesh_mask_from_AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/bdy_mask.nc" . ln -s "$DOMAIN_INPUTS/domain_cfg.nc" . ln -s "$DOMAIN_INPUTS/bathy_meter.nc" . Input Purpose AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc and mesh_mask_from_AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc AMM7 parent grid and wet-cell mask domain_cfg.nc and bathy_meter.nc Celtic Sea target grid and September bathymetry bdy_mask.nc Celtic Sea open-boundary mask. Cells marked -1 are outside the open boundary, 1 marks the active domain, and 0 marks land or closed areas. grid_name_map_sco.json NetCDF variable names for the source and target grids, both configured as sco Keep ln_mask_file = .true. to read the saved mask and ln_coords_file = .true. to write coordinates.bdy.nc . The mask, together with nn_rimwidth = 9 , defines the boundary points and their ordering. 3. Set the data paths in the namelist Edit these two entries in the copied namelist_AMM7CELTIC.bdy . sn_src_dir = '/path/to/pyBDY/inputs/src_data_local.ncml' sn_tide_fes = '/path/to/FES2014/' sn_src_dir points to a readable NcML file. pyBDY opens the source reader before extracting tides. The September run used src_data_local.ncml under the archived pyBDY inputs/ directory. Keep that file beside its benchmark/data/ folder so its relative paths resolve. sn_tide_fes points to your Cirrus copy of the FES2014 data directory. The archive links to the old ARCHER2 copy. Use the extrapolated elevation and both current components in ocean_tide_extrapolated/ , eastward_velocity/ , and northward_velocity/ . Each directory should contain the constituent files, for example m2.nc . AVISO FES data access Keep ln_tide = .true. , sn_tide_model = 'FES2014' , and ln_trans = .true. . The archived setup disables the time-varying barotropic, baroclinic, tracer, and ice outputs. The dates in the namelist do not limit the use of the tidal harmonics to those years. 4. Run pyBDY on Cirrus Save the following as submitpynemo.slurm in the working directory. Set the project account and the path to your Conda installation on a filesystem accessible to compute nodes. The job starts one pyBDY process. It requests 25 cores to allow roughly the same memory as the original 64 GB ARCHER2 request on a standard Cirrus node. Cirrus resource limits #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --job-name=pybdy_tide #SBATCH --account=YOUR_PROJECT #SBATCH --partition=standard #SBATCH --qos=standard #SBATCH --time=02:00:00 #SBATCH --ntasks=1 #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=25 set -e cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR" source /path/to/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh conda activate pybdy export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/jre-11 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 mkdir -p output_20260922 pybdy -s namelist_AMM7CELTIC.bdy Submit from the directory containing the namelist. sbatch submitpynemo.slurm 5. Check the output The September namelist writes to output_20260922/ . Expect coordinates.bdy.nc and 72 tidal NetCDF files , one per grid (T, U and V) for each of the 24 constituents. For example, the M2 files are named CELTIC_bdytide_FES2014_M2_grid_T.nc and similarly for U and V. ls -lh output_20260922/coordinates.bdy.nc find output_20260922 -maxdepth 1 -name 'CELTIC_bdytide_FES2014_*_grid_[TUV].nc' | wc -l The 1993 test-run script links files from the forcing bundle's TIDES/ directory and uses OBC/coordinates.bdy.nc at the run-directory root. The NEMO namelist reads the prefix ./TIDES/CELTIC_bdytide_FES2014_ . When substituting regenerated harmonics, check that their boundary points and ordering still match the coordinates used by the monthly AMM7 boundary files. The archived tidal coordinates and the forcing bundle's boundary coordinates have identical NetCDF variable values.

docs.text: From a checkout of pyBDY, create the Conda environment and install the package. The environment file specifies Python 3.9. The NcML reader also needs Java. pyBDY repository conda env create -n pybdy -f environment.yml conda activate pybdy python -m pip install -e . pybdy -h

docs.text: Set ARCHIVED_RUN to the path of your copy of CELTIC8_GEE_SF12_cutout . Set DOMAIN_INPUTS to the directory containing the matching domain_cfg.nc and bathy_meter.nc , such as the backup_260921_GEG_SF12_cutout domain archive. The original links in the pyBDY archive point to ARCHER2 /work paths. Create fresh links to the Cirrus copies. From the Celtic Sea checkout's Scripts/ directory, load the paths and prepare a working directory. source ./1.make_path.sh ARCHIVED_RUN=/path/to/CELTIC8_GEE_SF12_cutout DOMAIN_INPUTS=/path/to/backup_260921_GEG_SF12_cutout mkdir -p "$WDIR/BUILD_CFG/OPEN_BOUNDARIES/GEG_SF12_cutout" cd "$WDIR/BUILD_CFG/OPEN_BOUNDARIES/GEG_SF12_cutout" cp "$ARCHIVED_RUN/namelist_AMM7CELTIC.bdy" . cp "$ARCHIVED_RUN/grid_name_map_sco.json" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/mesh_mask_from_AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc" . ln -s "$ARCHIVED_RUN/bdy_mask.nc" . ln -s "$DOMAIN_INPUTS/domain_cfg.nc" . ln -s "$DOMAIN_INPUTS/bathy_meter.nc" . Input Purpose AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc and mesh_mask_from_AMM7_domain_cfg_sub.nc AMM7 parent grid and wet-cell mask domain_cfg.nc and bathy_meter.nc Celtic Sea target grid and September bathymetry bdy_mask.nc Celtic Sea open-boundary mask. Cells marked -1 are outside the open boundary, 1 marks the active domain, and 0 marks land or closed areas. grid_name_map_sco.json NetCDF variable names for the source and target grids, both configured as sco Keep ln_mask_file = .true. to read the saved mask and ln_coords_file = .true. to write coordinates.bdy.nc . The mask, together with nn_rimwidth = 9 , defines the boundary points and their ordering.
